title: Scientists Use ‘Grand Theft Auto’ to Model the Effects of Climate Change
gist: Researchers Paul Nörenberg and Hugues Lantuit built a flood model from GTA V's terrain of Los Santos and projected sea-level rise under IPCC RCP 2.6 and 8.5 scenarios; the game's vulnerable areas matched real Los Angeles flood hotspots. The piece also notes Rockstar's GTA franchise scale (465 million units, $3.79 billion GTA VI first-day sales).

insights.claim: Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto franchise has sold an estimated 465 million units worldwide, and GTA VI earned $3.79 billion in first-day sales.

insights.claim: Under the high-emissions RCP 8.5 scenario with storm surge, a flood model built on GTA V's Los Santos terrain projects water levels of 5.18 meters and 5.1% of land flooded by 2300, rising to 8.22 meters and 6.5% by 2500, hitting the port, wastewater and coastal energy infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Fernanda González
insights.so_what: Ports and coastal energy assets are the infrastructure most exposed in high-emissions flood scenarios.

insights.claim: Under the emissions-reduction RCP 2.6 scenario, the GTA V-based model shows only 2.2% of Los Santos flooded by 2300 with no major infrastructure affected.
insights.speaker: Fernanda González
insights.so_what: Mitigation pathway sharply cuts modeled coastal infrastructure damage.

insights.claim: The areas flagged as vulnerable in the GTA V model matched the three real Los Angeles locations most likely to flood: Venice Beach, Pacific Palisades and the Port of Los Angeles.
insights.speaker: Fernanda González
insights.so_what: Port of Los Angeles is a recurring flood-risk hotspot in climate modeling.

insights.claim: The researchers caution the GTA V model is not an exact prediction because it omits wave motion, beach erosion, currents and terrain changes.

insights.claim: The researchers argue a climate model set in a game world millions of people have explored can make climate impacts feel closer to reality, giving commercial game worlds value as science-communication tools.
insights.speaker: Fernanda González
insights.so_what: Detailed commercial game worlds have emerging secondary uses as digital twins for research and communication.
